chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, through his chain of transmission, he said:

A man was brought before al-Maʾmūn who had pushed another man into a well and he died, so he ordered that he be killed. The man said: “I was in my house when I heard the cry for help, so I came out quickly with my sword. I passed by this man while he was at the edge of a well, so I pushed him and he fell into the well.” Al-Maʾmūn asked the jurists about that. Some of them said retaliation should be taken against him, and some of them said this and that should be done to him. So he asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about that and wrote to him, and he replied: “His blood money is upon the people of the cry for help, those who shouted for help.”

He said: The jurists considered that very grave, and they said to al-Maʾmūn: “Ask him from where you said this.” So he asked, and he عليه السلام said: “A woman once sought judgment from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام against a wind. She said: ‘I was on top of my house, and a wind pushed me so I fell into the courtyard and my hand was broken.’ So Sulaymān عليه السلام summoned the wind and said to it: ‘What made you do what you did to this woman?’ The wind said: ‘O Prophet of Allah, the ship of such-and-such people was in the sea, and its people were on the verge of drowning. I passed by this woman while I was hurrying, so she fell and her hand was broken.’ Then Sulaymān عليه السلام ruled that the compensation for her hand was upon the people of the ship.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ السَّفِينَةِ: the people of the ship upon whom liability was placed
key_terms.الْغَوْثَ: the cry for help or rescue call that triggered the event
key_terms.بِأَرْشِ يَدِهَا: the assessed compensation for her injured hand
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: his blood money; the financial compensation due for wrongful killing
key_terms.يُقَادُ بِهِ: retaliation is carried out against him; qiṣāṣ

ai.seo_question: Who bears the diyah when someone is harmed indirectly while responding to a cry for help?
ai.summary: This narration concerns a judicial ruling about liability when harm occurs indirectly in the course of responding to an urgent cry for help. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام assigns the diyah to those whose call for rescue caused the chain of events, and supports the ruling with a precedent from the judgment of Sulaymān عليه السلام.
